Meta.title: Retroloop — sprint retros where action items get done
Meta.description: Run your sprint retrospective in the browser and make sure the action items actually get done. Free, no sign-up for anyone.

Landing.headline: Retros that actually change something
Landing.lead: Run your retrospective in the browser — and make sure the action items get done. Nobody needs an account: start a board, share the link.
Landing.problemTitle: The same problems, sprint after sprint
Landing.problem: Most teams finish less than half of the action items from their retros. The board is the easy part; what happens after it is where retros fail. Retroloop is built around that part.

write.title: Write, anonymously
write.body: Everyone adds cards. Other people's cards stay on the server until the facilitator reveals them — not just blurred on screen.

group.title: Group and vote
group.body: Drag similar cards together, then spend a limited number of votes on what matters most.

discuss.title: Agree on up to three actions
discuss.body: Each action item needs an owner and a due date. A few owned items get done; long lists don't.

review.title: Check them next time
review.body: The next retro opens with last time's items — done, not yet, or dropped — and your team's follow-through score.

features.noSignup: No sign-up for anyone, including the facilitator
features.realtime: Live for everyone: cards, votes and the timer stay in sync
features.exports: Export to Jira (CSV), GitHub issues, Markdown and calendar events
features.mobile: Works on a phone, for people joining from anywhere
features.privacy: No tracking cookies and no ads; hosted in the EU

Privacy.title: Privacy
Privacy.intro: Retroloop is built to need as little data as possible. There are no accounts, no tracking cookies and no ads.
Privacy.store: The team name, the names people type when they join, cards, votes, action items with their owners and due dates, and answers to the end-of-retro survey. Nothing else is asked for: no email, no password.
Privacy.browser: Your browser keeps your name and a secret key per retro (so a reload brings you back as yourself) in local storage. These are not cookies and are never used for tracking.
Privacy.analytics: To learn whether Retroloop helps, it counts events such as "a retro was created" or "a card was added". These counts never include names, card text, IP addresses or browser details.
Privacy.retention: A team's data is deleted automatically once it has not started a retro for 12 months. The facilitator can delete a retro, and everything in it, at any time from its wrap-up screen.
